free_tier.stated: no free tier; the cheapest plan, gc.pico, is USD 2.50/mo (USD 0.0034 per hour): 1 vCPU, 512 MB RAM, 20 GB disk, 2.5 Gbps port, 2 TB transfer; new accounts add one month of credit up front and servers then bill by the hour from that credit
free_tier.notes: the monthly figure is a 730-hour equivalent of the hourly rate; billing is against prepaid credit that has no expiry

retention.stated: a server runs and bills hourly from prepaid credit until it is destroyed; stopping it keeps the CPU, RAM and disk reserved and keeps the charge; credit has no expiry
retention.notes: behaviour when the credit balance reaches zero: unverified, not stated on the pages captured

egress.terms: 2 TB account transfer pool per UTC calendar month, plus each server's plan allowance (2 TB on gc.pico) earned prorated by time provisioned and shared across the account; beyond the pool, USD 3.00 per TB
egress.free_allowance: 2 TB per account per UTC calendar month plus the plan allowance (2 TB on gc.pico), prorated by time provisioned

interface_detail: root SSH credentials are issued when the server is provisioned; a browser VNC console is included; the portal Settings page lists API keys, and the API reference is unverified
tooling: SSH to a KVM guest with root; Debian, Ubuntu, Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux, Alpine Linux, FreeBSD, Windows (BYOL) and pfSense templates at checkout
chaining: Always-on KVM guest with a dedicated IPv4 and a pooled monthly transfer allowance, payable without a card by USDC stablecoin, Alipay or ACH.

limits.value: 2 TB per account per UTC calendar month plus 2 TB for gc.pico, prorated by time provisioned; USD 3.00 per TB beyond

limits_note: IPv6 is not available; one region (Tampa, Florida); no object storage and no attachable block volumes
binding_note: the pooled transfer is the first byte ceiling: 2 TB per account plus the plan allowance, then USD 3.00 per TB

identity_cost.detail: registration takes an email address and a password; first name, last name and business name are optional; the form shows no phone or ID document field; deployment needs prepaid credit (a single top-up is USD 3.00 to USD 1,000.00) or a saved card, and payment is accepted by card, wallet (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App Pay, Amazon Pay, Alipay), USDC stablecoin or US bank transfer (ACH); whether a payment or fraud check asks for more is unverified

reliability_note: single site: all servers and the optional backups are in Tampa, Florida, and backups live on the same cluster as the guest; a 99.9% SLA is stated; unverified: no incident or status history captured
confidence_note: price, shape, location, billing and the registration form are read from first-party pages and quoted; the pricing FAQ and the add-credit page disagree on PayPal, one saying it is accepted for one-time credit purchases and the other saying it is not accepted; any phone or ID check beyond the form is unverified

evidence.proved: gc.pico is the smallest plan: 1 vCPU, 512 MB RAM, 20 GB disk, 2.5 Gbps port, 2 TB transfer
evidence.quote: gc.pico 1 vCPU · 512 MB RAM · 20 GB disk · 2.5 Gbps · 2 TB transfer The lightest bots, probes, and tiny Linux services.

evidence.proved: gc.pico costs $2.50 a month and $0.0034 an hour
new accounts add one month of credit up front and servers then bill hourly from that credit
evidence.quote: New accounts add one month of credit up front; servers then bill by the hour from that credit.

evidence.proved: no setup fee and no minimum contract
evidence.quote: No setup fees and no minimum contract.

evidence.proved: transfer beyond the pool is USD 3.00 per TB
evidence.quote: Transfer beyond your pool bills at the same $3.00/TB.

evidence.proved: the transfer pool is 2 TB per account per UTC calendar month plus each server's plan allowance, prorated and shared
evidence.quote: Transfer starts with 2 TB included per account each UTC calendar month. Each server then earns its plan's transfer allowance over the month, prorated by time provisioned and shared across every server.

evidence.proved: every plan states a 99.9% SLA, root access and DDoS protection
evidence.quote: Every plan includes DDoS, root access, and the 99.9% SLA.

evidence.proved: the pricing FAQ states that PayPal is available for one-time credit purchases and monthly credit subscriptions
evidence.quote: PayPal is available for one-time credit purchases and monthly credit subscriptions.

evidence.proved: the server provisions automatically and root SSH credentials are issued on completion of the order
evidence.quote: Once your order completes, the VPS provisions automatically and you get root SSH credentials immediately.

evidence.proved: the only region is Tampa, Florida, on KVM with Xeon Scalable CPUs and NVMe storage
evidence.quote: Everything deploys in Tampa, Florida, on KVM, on Intel Xeon Scalable CPUs with Enterprise NVMe SSD storage.

evidence.proved: no IPv6, no load balancer, no object storage and no attachable block volumes
evidence.quote: Plan around these current product boundaries: there is no IPv6, no load balancer product, no object storage, and no block storage volumes you can attach and detach.

evidence.proved: a stopped server keeps its reservation and its charge; only destroying it stops billing
evidence.quote: Stopping it does not help, because the CPU, RAM and disk stay reserved for you. Destroying it is what stops the charge.

evidence.proved: the monthly figure on the pricing page is a 730-hour equivalent of the hourly rate
evidence.quote: The monthly figure on the pricing page is a 730 hour equivalent, published so you can compare plans against other hosts.

evidence.proved: snapshots and backups live on the same cluster as the guest
evidence.quote: They live on the same cluster as the guest.

evidence.proved: the account is identified by an email address alone, with no username
evidence.quote: There is no username: the account is the email address, so use the one you want receipts, provisioning credentials and support replies to reach.

evidence.proved: the portal Settings page lists API keys among its entries
evidence.quote: | Settings | Organization, members, workspaces, single sign-on, API keys, profile, appearance, privacy, password, two-factor, and sessions |

evidence.proved: the registration form asks for an email address and a password; first name, last name and business name are optional; no phone or ID field is shown
evidence.quote:

evidence.proved: a single credit top-up is between USD 3.00 and USD 1,000.00
evidence.quote: A single top-up is between $3.00 and $1,000.00.

evidence.proved: credit can be added before deploying, or a card saved, in which case deployment charges one month of the plan before the server is queued
evidence.quote: You can add that credit before you deploy, or save a usable card: with no available credit, deployment charges one month of credit for the selected plan before the server is queued.

evidence.proved: credit can be paid by card, wallets including Alipay, or US bank transfer (ACH)
evidence.quote: Cards and wallets: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Cash App Pay, Amazon Pay, and Alipay. US bank transfer (ACH) is available for credit top-ups.

evidence.proved: USDC stablecoin is accepted on Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, Base and Tempo
evidence.quote: - USDC on Ethereum, Solana, Polygon, Base, and Tempo

evidence.proved: the add-credit page states PayPal is not accepted, contradicting the pricing FAQ
evidence.quote: We do not accept PayPal, and crypto checkout settles the three stablecoins above and nothing else.

evidence.proved: credit has no expiry and there is no monthly minimum
evidence.quote: There is no expiry on credit and no monthly minimum.

notes: Hourly metering against prepaid credit; the monthly figure on the pricing page is a 730-hour equivalent of the hourly rate. A single region, Tampa, Florida.
